summary.text: BP was founded in 1909 as the Anglo-Persian Oil Company, renamed Anglo-Iranian Oil Company (AIOC) in 1935 and British Petroleum in 1954. Iran nationalized AIOC's operations in 1951. In August 1953, a coup planned and executed with the CIA and British intelligence overthrew Prime Minister Mohammad Mosaddeq. Under a 1954 agreement, AIOC took a 40% share in a new consortium that ran Iran's oil operations. In 2004, as part of an Ogilvy & Mather advertising campaign, BP launched a personal 'carbon footprint calculator', which critics say shifted attention from producers to consumers.

sources.title: CIA Confirms Role in 1953 Iran Coup

facts.claim: After Iran nationalized the assets of the Anglo-Iranian Oil Company in 1951, the CIA and British intelligence (SIS) planned and carried out Operation TPAJAX, the coup that overthrew Prime Minister Mohammad Mosaddeq on August 19, 1953.

facts.claim: BP, which hired the public relations firm Ogilvy & Mather for its 'Beyond Petroleum' campaign, unveiled a personal 'carbon footprint calculator' in 2004 and promoted the term 'carbon footprint'. Critics, including historian Benjamin Franta, describe the campaign as shifting attention from oil companies to individual consumers.

connections.claim: After Iran nationalized the Anglo-Iranian Oil Company (BP's predecessor) in 1951, the CIA and British intelligence organized the August 1953 coup that removed Prime Minister Mosaddeq. Under a 1954 agreement with the post-coup government, AIOC took a 40% interest in the consortium operating Iran's oil industry and received compensation.
